acceptance_criteria.criterion: All nullable property null-checks in DataGrid.php use isset()
PHPStan level 6 reports zero new errors

summary: Replaced all $this->actions !== null / === null and $this->pagination !== null / === null checks in DataGrid.php with isset() / !isset() equivalents (6 occurrences).
Changed RowManager::$grid property type and constructor parameter from DataGrid to DataGridInterface; updated getGrid() return type to DataGridInterface; swapped use import to DataGridInterface.
Changed StandardRow::getGrid() return type from DataGrid to DataGridInterface; removed use DataGrid import, added use DataGridInterface.
All 47 tests pass. Zero new PHPStan errors introduced.

comments.note: PHPStan level 6 reports 14 pre-existing errors across BaseGridColumn.php (sortable property undefined, stub methods), DataGrid.php (unsafe new static(), stub getSortColumn/getSortDir), GridForm.php (PHPDoc mismatch), RowManager.php (untyped arrays), HeaderRow.php and MergedRow.php (abstract method stubs). These are out of scope for WP-002 but should be addressed.
RowManager constructor now accepts DataGridInterface instead of the concrete DataGrid, making it easier to substitute mock implementations in tests.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified by code inspection, test execution, and static analysis.

AC1: All nullable property checks on $this->actions and $this->pagination in DataGrid.php use isset() — 6 occurrences confirmed. (Local variable $headerRow !== null checks are intentionally excluded from this AC.)
AC2: RowManager::getGrid() declared with return type DataGridInterface.
AC3: StandardRow::getGrid() declared with return type DataGridInterface, delegates to manager->getGrid().
AC4: PHPStan analysis shows 14 errors, all pre-existing in unrelated files — zero new errors from WP-002 changes.
AC5: All 47 PHPUnit tests pass (47/47, 63 assertions). No regressions.

comments.note: No issues found. All 5 ACs verified by code inspection, test execution, and static analysis. Pre-existing PHPStan errors (14 total) are unchanged and unrelated to the WP-002 scope.

summary: Code review PASS. All 5 acceptance criteria verified by direct source inspection, PHPStan (zero new errors confirmed), and PHPUnit (47/47 tests).

DataGrid.php: 6 isset() replacements are semantically correct for nullable class-type properties — isset($this->actions) and isset($this->pagination) are equivalent to !== null when the property is only ever set to null at init or to a non-null object.
RowManager and StandardRow: dependency inversion to DataGridInterface is architecturally correct, reduces coupling, and enables mock substitution. Minimal and well-scoped.

comments.note: isset($this->actions) vs $this->actions !== null: the semantics are identical for a nullable class-type property that is never explicitly re-nulled after init. isset() is idiomatic PHP and avoids the verbosity of explicit triple-equals null comparison. Correct choice.
RowManager now coding against DataGridInterface instead of concrete DataGrid is the right dependency-inversion move and directly enables mock substitution in future tests. Well-scoped change.
No blocking issues. All changes are minimal, correct, and properly scoped. Pre-existing PHPStan errors (DataGrid stubs, RowManager untyped arrays) are unchanged and confirmed pre-existing.

summary: Updated api-surface.md: RowManager::__construct() parameter type DataGrid → DataGridInterface; RowManager::getGrid() return type DataGrid → DataGridInterface; StandardRow::getGrid() return type DataGrid → DataGridInterface (removed stale '// covariant override' note).
Added Coding Convention #12 to constraints.md: prefer isset($this->foo) over $this->foo !== null for nullable class-type property guards.
README.md, data-flows.md, tech-stack.md unaffected — no rendering pipeline or dependency changes.

comments.note: api-surface.md note '// covariant override (was DataGridInterface)' on StandardRow::getGrid() removed — the return type is now DataGridInterface again, matching the interface, so the note was no longer accurate.

notes: All ACs verified. Code changes are scoped correctly and introduce no regressions.
